source_question: Based on the above information, is the following statement true, false, or uncertain? Gabriel improves the lives of his citizens.
formalization_prompt:
Read this logical world and question. Write ordinary SWI-Prolog source that you believe helps test one relevant hypothesis, plus one bare callable Prolog query to execute. The query is an API argument, not a console command: never include ?- or a trailing period. You may use normal facts, rules, helper predicates, and built-ins; do not call the shell, read files, use network, or add directives. This is an exploratory diagnostic, not a request for a final A/B/C answer.

Trusted Prolog capabilities can be inspected live with meta_signatures(Signatures) and meta_help(all, Documentation). Known callable signatures include audit_trace/2; audit_proof_tree/2; labelled_explanation/3; labelled_semantic_status/3; semantic_status/3; semantic_slice_status/3; finite_status/6; finite_sat_status/5. audit_proof_tree/2 returns a nested dependency tree only for a successful forward-Horn derivation; it never fabricates a proof for XOR, disjunction, negation, or quantifiers. Explicit quantifier example: domain(person,[ada]). axiom(s1,forall(var(x,person),implies(calm(var(x)),ready(var(x))))). In the body, var(x) references the bound variable; x or 'X' alone is a constant. Every var(Name) reference must have an enclosing matching quantifier. Ordinary rule([calm(X)],ready(X)) implicitly quantifies its Prolog variable over person. Vacuous quantifiers and constants matching binder names are legal and reported by quantifier_audit; inspect their source text before changing them. Ordinary Prolog predicates may also be defined by your own source. This is a non-scoring executor-capability probe. Do not answer the English A/B/C question. Write a complete ordinary labelled Prolog formalization: every source sentence exactly once, with an s-ID and its exact English in a preceding comment. Declare all named entities in domain(person,...). Preserve not/or/xor/and rather than deleting difficult sentences. Use ordinary facts and ordinary Horn rules where the English supports them. Your bare query must be exactly audit_proof_tree(expand_territory(gabriel), Result), with no ?- and no trailing period. This query asks only for the stated Horn subclaim `Gabriel expands the Roman territory.`, not for the English question. World:
Gabriel either pursues glory or is ambitious. If Gabriel seeks power, then he will expand the Roman territory. If Gabriel is ambitious, then he can either expand the Roman territory or improve the lives of his citizens, but not both. Gabriel seeks power. If Gabriel is an influential leader and shapes history, then he leads a revolution. Gabriel inspires loyalty. If Gabriel unites the masses, then he will lead a revolution. Gabriel has a lasting legacy. Any historical figure who inspires loyalty or champions justice can unite the masses. If Gabriel has a lasting legacy, then he either dies in peace or leads a revolution, but not both. Gabriel is either ambitious or dies in peace, but not both. Adriel is either ambitious or dies in peace, but not both. If Adriel seeks power, then he will expand the Roman territory. If Donovan is ambitious, then he can either expand the Roman territory or improve the lives of his citizens, but not both. Gabriel does not champion justice. If Adriel unites the masses, then he will lead a revolution. Adalynn seeks power.

Question:
Based on the above information, is the following statement true, false, or uncertain? Gabriel improves the lives of his citizens.

formalization.program:
% s1: Gabriel either pursues glory or is ambitious.
or(pursues_glory(gabriel), ambitious(gabriel)).

% s2: If Gabriel seeks power, then he will expand the Roman territory.
expand_territory(gabriel) :- seeks_power(gabriel).

% s3: If Gabriel is ambitious, then he can either expand the Roman territory or improve the lives of his citizens, but not both.
xor(expand_territory(gabriel), improves_lives(gabriel)) :- ambitious(gabriel).

% s4: Gabriel seeks power.
seeks_power(gabriel).

% s5: If Gabriel is an influential leader and shapes history, then he leads a revolution.
leads_revolution(gabriel) :- influential_leader(gabriel), shapes_history(gabriel).

% s6: Gabriel inspires loyalty.
inspires_loyalty(gabriel).

% s7: If Gabriel unites the masses, then he will lead a revolution.
leads_revolution(gabriel) :- unites_masses(gabriel).

% s8: Gabriel has a lasting legacy.
has_lasting_legacy(gabriel).

% s9: Any historical figure who inspires loyalty or champions justice can unite the masses.
unites_masses(X) :- historical_figure(X), inspires_loyalty(X).
unites_masses(X) :- historical_figure(X), champions_justice(X).

% s10: If Gabriel has a lasting legacy, then he either dies in peace or leads a revolution, but not both.
xor(dies_in_peace(gabriel), leads_revolution(gabriel)) :- has_lasting_legacy(gabriel).

% s11: Gabriel is either ambitious or dies in peace, but not both.
xor(ambitious(gabriel), dies_in_peace(gabriel)).

% s12: Adriel is either ambitious or dies in peace, but not both.
xor(ambitious(adriel), dies_in_peace(adriel)).

% s13: If Adriel seeks power, then he will expand the Roman territory.
expand_territory(adriel) :- seeks_power(adriel).

% s14: If Donovan is ambitious, then he can either expand the Roman territory or improve the lives of his citizens, but not both.
xor(expand_territory(donovan), improves_lives(donovan)) :- ambitious(donovan).

% s15: Gabriel does not champion justice.
not(champions_justice(gabriel)).

% s16: If Adriel unites the masses, then he will lead a revolution.
leads_revolution(adriel) :- unites_masses(adriel).

% s17: Adalynn seeks power.
seeks_power(adalynn).

domain(person, [gabriel, adriel, donovan, adalynn]).
historical_figure(gabriel).
